record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
record.original_question: Given any paratopological group (G, tau), where tau is a Hausdorff topology making multiplication continuous, does there always exist a coarser or equal group topology tau' <= tau such that (G, tau') is a topological group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A paratopological group is a pair $(G,\tau)$ consisting of a group $G$ equipped with a topology $\tau$ such that the multiplication map $G\times G\to G$, $(x,y)\mapsto xy$, is jointly continuous (inversion is not required to be continuous). A topological group is a paratopological group $(G,\tau')$ in which, additionally, the inversion map $x\mapsto x^{-1}$ is continuous.

Question: Let $(G,\tau)$ be an arbitrary paratopological group whose topology $\tau$ is Hausdorff. Does there always exist a group topology $\tau'$ on $G$ with $\tau'\subseteq\tau$ (i.e., $\tau'$ is coarser than or equal to $\tau$) such that $(G,\tau')$ is a topological group?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface considerable activity on related questions (e.g., when a Hausdorff/first-countable paratopological group admits a coarser (separable) metrizable group topology, regularity vs. complete regularity of paratopological groups), but no source found directly resolves the general question of whether every Hausdorff paratopological group admits a coarser group topology making it a topological group. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Each regular paratopological group is completely regular
status_evidence.snippet: Banakh–Ravsky type result on regularity properties of paratopological groups, related to coarser-topology questions.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related results exist but do not resolve the stated question.

status_evidence.title: Simply sm-factorizable (para)topological groups and their completions
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of strongly submetrizable (para)topological groups admitting coarser metrizable group topologies.
status_evidence.claim: Related coarser-topology questions are studied; the general Hausdorff case is not addressed conclusively here.
